Application Questions

Respondents will be asked to address the following 1 questions.

How many enumerators can you field in Kaura, and what is your experience running household coverage surveys?

Optional
Evaluation Criteria

Responses will be scored across 5 criteria. Weights reflect the relative importance of each area.

Survey Methodology Rigor
30%

Evaluates the technical soundness of the proposed household sampling and enumeration approach for verifying vitamin-A delivery across R6 matched wards.

What makes a strong response?

Strong responses detail a statistically valid household sampling framework specifically addressing both the intervention (Attakar) and match (Gura) areas, include rooftop-level verification protocols, and describe how enumerators will confirm vitamin-A delivery. Weak responses offer generic survey methods without addressing the matched-ward design, lack rooftop sampling specifics, or fail to distinguish between intervention and comparison areas.
Enumerator Qualifications
25%

Assesses the experience, training plan, and supervisory structure of field enumerators who will conduct independent household verification visits.

What makes a strong response?

Strong responses demonstrate prior experience conducting independent coverage surveys in comparable geographic or programmatic contexts, include a clear training curriculum for rooftop-level vitamin-A verification, and outline supervisor-to-enumerator ratios. Weak responses provide vague staffing plans, lack evidence of relevant field experience, or do not address quality control during enumeration.
Geographic Coverage Plan
20%

Evaluates the respondent's plan to systematically cover all sampled rooftops across both the Attakar intervention area and the Gura match area within the R6 plan group.

What makes a strong response?

Strong responses present a clear geographic mapping strategy that accounts for both R6 matched ward areas, include contingency plans for hard-to-reach households, and demonstrate understanding of the Attakar × Gura coverage zones. Weak responses treat the survey area as a single undifferentiated zone, overlook one of the paired areas, or lack logistical detail for reaching all sampled households.
Data Quality Assurance
15%

Assesses the processes proposed to ensure accuracy, consistency, and independence of vitamin-A delivery verification data collected at the household level.

What makes a strong response?

Strong responses describe specific data validation steps such as back-checks, duplicate entry, or independent re-verification of a sample of rooftops, and explain how enumerator independence from the delivery program will be maintained. Weak responses mention quality assurance only in general terms, do not address the independence requirement of the survey, or lack re-verification mechanisms.
Reporting and Timeline
10%

Evaluates the clarity, feasibility, and completeness of the proposed reporting structure and schedule for delivering survey findings from the R6 matched-ward coverage assessment.

What makes a strong response?

Strong responses include a realistic, detailed timeline with milestones tied to field enumeration and data analysis phases, specify deliverable formats that allow comparison between Attakar and Gura areas, and identify key reporting contacts. Weak responses provide only a final report date without intermediate milestones, do not address how matched-ward comparisons will be presented, or offer an implausibly compressed or vague schedule.
